name: MSU Zagreb (Museum of Contemporary Art)
funding: City of Zagreb; listed sponsors include public companies ZET and HRT.

name: Nicosia Municipal Arts Centre (NiMAC)
funding: Nicosia Municipality and the Pierides Foundation run it under a cooperation agreement. Shows credit the Deputy Ministry of Culture, A.G. Leventis Foundation and European University Cyprus. No budget is published.

name: Brummel House (Adolf Loos in Pilsen)
funding: The Brummel family owns the house. Plzeň - TURISMUS, a City of Pilsen organisation, runs the tours. The Adolf Loos Plzeň project credits Ministry for Regional Development state-budget money.

name: Fondation Donwahi
funding: Founder Illa Donwahi's own funds (agribusiness), private patrons and annual partner grants.

name: Musée des Cultures Contemporaines Adama Toungara (MuCAT)
funding: Built on the initiative of Adama Toungara, then mayor of Abobo; the director says it was built from own funds.

name: Kin ArtStudio
funding: Small artist-run residency (active 2024); housed in the TEXAF concession, with Pro Helvetia residencies and Fondation Montresso partnership.

name: Texaf Bilembo
funding: Texaf, listed on Euronext Brussels, is founder and head sponsor of the centre. Its income is 85% Kinshasa real estate, 12% a sandstone quarry and 3% digital.

name: Picha / Lubumbashi Biennale
funding: Founders' own money, private donors and Belgian and French agencies. 2026 Biennale sponsors: Belgian foreign ministry, Wallonie-Bruxelles, Enabel, Africalia, Pullman, Africell, TMB bank.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Santo Domingo
funding: State museum run by the Dominican Ministry of Culture on the Plaza de la Cultura; its director sits on the ministry's Bienal Nacional commission.

name: Museo Antropológico y de Arte Contemporáneo (MAAC)
funding: Ecuador's Culture vice-ministry (merged into Education in 2025) runs and funds it on a budget above USD 2.5M, and pays the city's Malecón 2000 foundation near USD 500,000 a year.

name: Museo Nacional del Ecuador (MuNa)
funding: State national museum; the government has budgeted about US$100M for a new building, with a state-owned enterprise managing construction.

name: 6th of October War Panorama
funding: Egypt's state commissioned it under President Mubarak and the National Military Museums Department runs it. North Korean architects helped build it; tickets cost 3 to 30 Egyptian pounds in 2010.
